before.title: Left dual and right dual object
The zig-zag identities
What 'left' refers to in 'left dual'
A left dual of an object has that object as a right dual
before.strategy: Reflect the left-dual data across the two zig-zag composites to build the mirrored evaluation and coevaluation, then verify the right-dual zig-zags by straightening the same string-diagram composites.

before.title: The unit is self-dual
before.strategy: Take the evaluation and coevaluation to be the unit isomorphism and its inverse, then read the two zig-zag identities as the monoidal triangle identities specialized to the tensor unit.

before.title: Reversing the tensor product exchanges left and right duals
before.strategy: Rewrite the left-dual zig-zags in the reverse monoidal structure and observe that the tensor-order reversal turns them exactly into the right-dual zig-zags, and conversely.

before.title: Duals are unique up to a unique compatible isomorphism
before.strategy: Compose the coevaluation of one dual with the evaluation of the other to define the comparison map, then use the zig-zag identities twice to prove both compatibility and uniqueness.

before.title: Duality yields adjunctions of tensoring functors
before.strategy: Transpose a map across the coevaluation and evaluation of a chosen dual object, prove the two transpose constructions are inverse, and then package them as the unit-counit data for the tensoring adjunctions.

before.title: A dual object in the endofunctor category is an adjoint functor
before.strategy: Read composition of endofunctors as the tensor product and compare the evaluation, coevaluation, and zig-zag identities term by term with the counit, unit, and triangle identities of an adjunction.

before.title: A second proof that adjoints are unique
before.strategy: Apply dual uniqueness inside the endofunctor-composition monoidal category, where left adjoints appear exactly as left duals of the same endofunctor.

before.title: Rigid object and rigid monoidal category
Not every monoidal category is rigid
before.strategy: Use an infinite-dimensional vector space V inside the monoidal category of all vector spaces: if coev(1)=sum v_i tensor f_i were finite, then the zig-zag identity would expand every vector v as a linear combination of the finitely many v_i, contradicting infinite dimension.

before.title: Finite-dimensional vector spaces are rigid
before.strategy: Work in the published monoidal category of modules over a field, choose a finite basis and dual basis, define coevaluation by the finite sum of basis vectors tensor dual basis vectors, and verify the two zig-zag identities by coordinate expansion.

before.title: The dual of a morphism
Left duality is a contravariant antimonoidal functor
before.strategy: Check that the transpose formula for f^vee preserves identities and reverses composition, then use uniqueness of duals together with the reversed tensor order on dual pairs to identify (X tensor Y)^vee with Y^vee tensor X^vee.

before.title: The double dual is a monoidal functor
before.strategy: Compose the contravariant antimonoidal left-duality functor with itself, so the two order reversals cancel and the induced comparison maps assemble into a monoidal endofunctor.

before.title: Left and right duals, and double duals, need not collapse
before.strategy: Follow the source warning that a rigid category can have nontrivial double-dual functors and nonisomorphic left and right duals; the authoring step either supplies one checked witness covering both failures or downgrades this scaffold to a recorded remark rather than inventing a witness.

before.title: In a rigid category every morphism of monoidal functors is an isomorphism
before.strategy: Use rigidity to manufacture candidate inverses to the component on each object by inserting duals and monoidal structure maps, then verify the two composites collapse by the monoidal naturality squares and the zig-zag identities.

before.title: A braided rigid category has a Drinfeld morphism

before.title: FALSE: the dimension of an object is independent of the pivotal structure

before.title: Fusion and multifusion categories
Tensor-category terminology follows the EGNO convention
Tensor product in a multitensor category is biexact
before.strategy: Use the left and right duals of a fixed tensor factor to exhibit both adjoints of each tensoring functor; their limit and colimit preservation, together with bilinearity, gives exactness in each variable.

before.title: Dualization in a multitensor category is exact
before.strategy: Use the contravariant duality equivalence to the opposite abelian category and transport short exact sequences through that equivalence, keeping the resulting kernel and cokernel comparison maps canonical.

before.title: Images commute with tensor products in a multitensor category
before.strategy: Factor each morphism through its image, tensor the epi and mono portions one variable at a time using biexactness, and identify the resulting canonical middle object with the image of the tensor product.

before.title: Tensoring with a dualizable object preserves projectives
before.strategy: Transport the relevant Hom functor across the tensor-dual adjunction and compose the projective Hom functor with the exact tensoring functor in the other variable.

before.title: The unit is projective exactly when the tensor category is semisimple
before.strategy: Apply projective preservation to the projective unit to make every object projective, then use the abelian semisimplicity criterion; the converse is immediate.

before.title: The unit object of a multitensor category is semisimple
before.strategy: Follow EGNO's unit-endomorphism and component argument: use image compatibility to obtain the finite indecomposable-unit decomposition, then use exact dualization and a simple subobject to prove that every component unit is simple.

before.title: The unit object of a tensor category is simple
before.strategy: Specialize the semisimple-unit decomposition to the canonical scalar map k to End(1): its being an isomorphism excludes more than one nonzero simple summand.

before.title: Evaluation is epic and coevaluation monic for nonzero objects
before.strategy: Use the simple unit and the two nonzero zig-zag composites: a nonzero map to the simple unit is epic, and a nonzero map from the simple unit is monic.

before.title: Tensor functors between tensor categories
An exact k-linear strong monoidal functor out of a tensor category is faithful
before.strategy: Use monicity of coevaluation to show that an exact strong monoidal functor kills no nonzero object, then apply exactness to the image of a morphism it kills.

before.title: The Grothendieck ring of a tensor category
Grothendieck-ring multiplication is well-defined
before.strategy: Use biexactness to send each short-exact relation to a relation in either tensor variable, so the tensor product descends to the quotient group; the associator and unitors supply the ring laws.

before.title: Fusion rules
Duality induces an anti-involution on the Grothendieck ring
before.strategy: Use exact dualization to descend [X] mapsto [X-vee] through short-exact relations and its antimonoidal structure to reverse products; apply double duality for the square.

before.title: Left and right dual objects are isomorphic in a semisimple multitensor category
before.strategy: Reduce to a simple object and characterize its left and right duals by the unique simple object producing a nonzero unit Hom; semisimplicity equates the two relevant Hom dimensions.

before.title: Objectwise double-dual isomorphisms do not supply a pivotal structure

Every finite k-linear abelian category is semisimple
before.strategy: Refute the asserted implication by separating the finite and semisimple clauses in the definitions and pointing to the nonsemisimple finite-category phenomenon recorded by the source.

before.title: Every rigid k-linear abelian monoidal category is a tensor category
before.strategy: Compare the assertion with the full tensor-category definition and exhibit the omitted local-finiteness, bilinearity, and scalar-unit hypotheses as independent requirements.

before.title: A tensor functor is just a strong monoidal functor
before.strategy: Compare the general strong-monoidal definition with the tensor-category convention, which also requires k-linearity, exactness, and faithfulness.

before.title: The Grothendieck ring of a tensor category is always commutative
before.strategy: Use the anti-involution formula to identify the available order reversal and explain that a braiding, not tensor-category structure alone, would supply commutativity.

before.title: Objectwise isomorphisms X isomorphic to its double dual supply a pivotal structure
before.strategy: Contrast an objectwise existence statement with the required monoidal natural isomorphism and identify naturality and monoidality as additional coherent data.
